limits: This is a source compatibility judgment, not execution equivalence, a new provider observation, or evidence that native model quality or learning improves.

Journal, setup and request-write time consume existing deadlines. Late readiness is rejected, and opt-in receive no longer has the legacy one-second floor. These stricter timing checks and added I/O overhead can change timeout outcomes despite unchanged nominal caps.
Best-effort flushed journals have no crash-durability guarantee. Missing stages do not establish zero inference usage, complete cleanup or a behavioral failure.

A network-isolated startup qualification sends no work request. Even nine successful starts do not revalidate provider inference or guarantee twenty-day world completion under shared resource and I/O contention.

Future dispatch must retain the original historical evidence hashes, exact reviewed current source maps, successful current-source nine-slot raw qualification, current installed dependency/binary checks and live boot/security-context/resource binding. Any unreviewed source change requires another review.
The six-world endpoint still requires all three valid completed pairs; failed or missing slots cannot be replaced by historical worlds or zero-valued future outcomes.
rationale: Historical native provider/tool/file capability remains an observation at its original exact source and must pass its original corrected raw audit.
The reviewed delta adds opt-in local startup and parent-pipe observations, process/source identifiers and explicit observation errors; it propagates the same option to online and learning replays.

The model and task prompts, trusted grader, filesystem/work protocol, native transport request construction, token/call meter, split chronology and SkillOpt adoption rules are unchanged in the bound library maps.

The observation flag is enabled equally in both prospective arms. Current-source startup and resource-boundary capability must be established by the separate complete nine-slot scope qualification before any full-world dispatch.
